reconcile.note: Gill reads Saul's suspicion in 18:9 and his enmity in 18:29 as one escalating hostility, not two rival starting points.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "When did Saul become David's enemy?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/become_enemies.html) (1999).

sides.snippet: Saul eyed David from that day and forward.
sides.verseText: Saul eyed David from that day and forward.

sides.snippet: Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul was David's enemy continually.
sides.verseText: Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul was David's enemy continually.
